label: text
text: Alleged to be strike pickets, two Chinese are facing a rather unusual prosecution in the Police Court as a sequel to a shooting incident over the New Territory border.

label: text
text: On the night of September 27, some men were loading a junk with vegetables to be smuggled into Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Armed pickets opened fire and the men dived into the river.

label: text
text: The boat was taken further down the river to strike headquarters.

label: text
text: Alleged to have been instigated by the powers that be, defendants are accused of having taken the vegetables into "Hong Kong for disposal, because "higher prices were obtainable here.

label: text
text: The two complainants in the case also came into Hong Kong—by another route—and traced their cargo.

label: text

label: text
text: Some of it had been sold to market stallholders but no money had been paid over and the goods were perishable.

label: text
text: When the case came before Major C. Willson this morning, Mr. G. R. Haywood appeared for the prosecution and Mr. D. McCallum for the defence. Chief Det.-Inspector T. Murphy was present for the Police.

label: text
text: In a discussion as to ball, Mr. Haywood ventured that if defendants had been pickets for any time, they would have no difficulty in raising the sum ($800 each). Mr. McCallum remarked that there was an "if" there and questioned about a third man—it having been alleged that three pickets were concerned with the incident.

label: text
text: Mr. Murphy declined to say whether the third man was in custody or would be charged. Hearing was to start this afternoon.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: QUESTION OF STANDARD RENT.

label: text
text: MORTGAGEE'S POSITION

label: text
text: The case was continued at the Summary Court this morning involving the position of a mortgagee who, in default of interest payment by the mortgagor, took over control of the premises in respect of which the mortgage was made only to find that rent in excess of standard rent had been paid to the mortgagor and that the tenants claimed to be entitled to refrain from paying further rent until the excess had been met.

label: text
text: Mak Tung-shi claims $1,000 (through her attorney, Ip Li-kong) from the National Optical Company, tenants of the premises in question, in respect of rent.

label: text
text: Mr. M. K. Lo is for plaintiffs and Mr. L. D. Turner for defendants.

label: text
text: When the case was heard this morning, Mr. Turner said that he had no further evidence to call as to what the rent was on the occasion of the first letting of the domestic tenements as a separate letting after December 31, 1920. At the last hearing His Honour had forced him (Mr. Turner) into an adjournment by holding that under section 2 of the Rents Ordinance, 1922, sub-section (g2), this clause was not the proper one for him to use to satisfy His Honour as to what the standard rent of these premises was.

label: paragraph_title
text: BOYCOTT END.

label: paragraph_title
text: His Honour's Mistake.

label: text
text: His Honour replied that he had read this judgment again and was prepared to admit that his interpretation at the last hearing had been at fault. The misunderstanding arose out of his taking the words "actually, let" as meaning "occupied". His views were still in accordance with the previous judgment.

label: text
text: This holding, said Mr. Turner, was contrary to a previous judgment which. His Honour himself had given.

label: text
text: Mr. Turner quoted sub section (g) referring to powers conferred in the event of the domestic, tenement not being let at the time but having been let at some previous date and held that the assessor's certificate which he had put in previously was some evidence that the tenement in question had been let on some previous date. It was some evidence of the standard rent and as it was all that the court had to go on he (Mr. Turner) claimed that it was sufficient.

label: text
text:

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Authentic news was received last night that the Canton Government is to call off the boycott, officially, at midday on October 10.

label: text
text:
The course proposed is attributed to a desire to get the necessary public atmosphere.
Pro-Kuomintang organisations will, it is stated, promote a procession on that day, to express support for the Government's decision.

label: text
text: At the east parade ground, the speakers are to include Mr. Eugene Chen and Mr. Chan Shuyan (Head of the Labour Department).

label: paragraph_title
text: Pickets Returning

label: text
text: At noon, the boycott will terminate with an announcement instead of a proclamation.

label: text
text: Meanwhile steps are being taken to withdraw all the strike pickets by that date.

label: text
text: A Canton paper says that the 5th detachment of pickets have all returned to Canton and that others are following suit.

label: text
text: It is thought that the present examination shed, run by the so-called Labour-Mercantile Association, is to be abolished.

label: text
text: Outwardly there is no change in the situation.

label: paragraph_title

text: officials are said to be working strenuously to remove opposition and lay down the details for the inaugural of the new era.

label: text
text: It is significant that influential bodies are still referring to the termination of the boycott as "the alteration in principal policy" and not as the end of the movement.

label: text
text: The only course now is to wait until the Republican holiday on October 10 and see what developments follow.

label: text
text: Best informed opinion is that the pickets will be demobilised and communications restored but that trade will still be hindered by an under-current of agitation.

This game of give and take is hard to explain. For want of a better example, the present situation may be best understood by supposing that a war was on between England and Scotland.
Sun Chuan-fang has advanced along the east coast and captured Edinburgh while Chang Kai-shek has come down the west coast and taken Manchester!

From Kfuklang (further down the river) it is reported that southern troops have reached Tean, 40 miles from Kfuklang and on the railway between Kfuklang and Nanchang; and that Marshal Sun Chuan-fang is withdrawing troops to that front from Hwangchow, where he has made an armistice with General Tang Sang-chee.

Note: General Tang Sang-chee commands the 8th Nationalist Army. As pretender to the fuchunship of Hunan, province, he practically caused the war, being driven right into Kwangtung until Chang Kalshel, espoused his cause. Since then he has marched victoriously.

Nervousness in Southern
Ranks?

label: text
text: Word of another southern advance has now come to hand and it is announced that Sun Chuan-fang's troops have arrived at the towns of Kiahui, west of Hwang-chow, and Nanchi, near the river.

label: text
text: This advance along the north bank of the Yangtse is significant in that it threatens Hwangchow. As a matter of fact quite an exodus of inhabitants from that place has taken place and some of these coming to Hankow report considerable nervousness apparent there.

label: text
text: This is not only in connection with the residents of the city but also witnessed in the ranks of the scuthern troops defending the place.

label: text
text: These, it seems, are chiefly composed of the 2nd division under Gen. Liu Tso-lung (who betrayed Hanyang) and part of them are said to have evacuated the city and are now on their way up to Han-kow.

label: paragraph_title
text: "Echo of Gunfire.

label: text
text: Reports coming in late last night state that the northern troops have moved their base on the north bank from Kichow to Kisui.

label: text
text: This would indicate that a considerable advance must have been made at this point. It was also intimated that a large detachment of troops had been warned at Hanyang to leave last night as (southein) reinforcements to Hwangchow.

label: text
text: Further proof that the northern forces are now rapidly advancing and are nearing Wu-Han is apparent in that very distant gun fire is clearly audible during the very early hours of the morning when the sound is not drowned by louder local noises. The detonations were distinctly heard yesterday morning, which shows that the northern forces are a good deal nearer than the reports say.

label: text
text: This, and the influx of refugees from the different fighting zones, has more or less spread the news of the retirement of the southern forces among the Chinese in the city, where it is now asserted that the northern forces will soon be in occupation here.

label: text
text:
The southern forces which were there have retired to Ngotsin and Tungshan and the concentration of troops in these places has caused the ordinary Chinese, who fear an early clash, to evacuate.
